accuracyFlags: FAQ: 'A standard car licence covers most combinations up to 4.5 tonnes gross combination mass': wrong measure. A car licence covers a vehicle up to 4.5 t GVM (heavier needs Light Rigid); the combination limit is the vehicle's own towing capacity, GCM rating and each state's trailer rules. Mislabelling GVM as GCM could mislead a driver.

FAQ speed: 'Western Australia and the Northern Territory hold towing vehicles to a lower limit': WA is correct (100 km/h), but sources show the NT applies the posted limit to caravans; NSW's 100 km/h cap applies to combinations over 4.5 t, which the body states correctly but the FAQ omits. Body and FAQ disagree.
'Exceeding your vehicle's rated tow capacity voids insurance regardless of licence': overstated, cover depends on policy and insurer.
'Western Australia ... 60-metre following rule behind certain heavy or towing vehicles': unverified; link the WA Road Traffic Code section.

'Ten percent of weight on the tow ball' is a rule of thumb (typically 8-15% depending on van): label as such. Page links WA, NSW and SA only; Vic, Qld, Tas, NT, ACT rules absent so 'state differences' in the title is under-delivered.
